Chief Executive Officer
Northgate Instrument Company
88 Foundry Row
Dayton, Ohio 45402

Re: Engagement for Representation — Trade Secret Litigation Against Cardinal Metrology, Inc.

Dear Ms. Raghunathan:

Thank you for asking Harlow & Vance LLP (the “Firm,” “we,” or “us”) to represent Northgate Instrument Company (the “Client,” “you”) in the above matter. This letter, together with the attached Standard Terms of Engagement, states the terms on which we will represent you. Please review it carefully, and if it is acceptable, sign and return the enclosed copy.

1. Scope of the Engagement.

We will represent you in connection with the investigation, prosecution, and, if appropriate, settlement of claims against Cardinal Metrology, Inc. arising from the alleged misappropriation of your coordinate-measurement calibration files (the “Matter”). Our representation is limited to the Matter. We are not undertaking to advise you on tax, accounting, insurance-coverage, employment, or regulatory matters, and we are not undertaking to represent any parent, subsidiary, affiliate, officer, director, or employee of the Client unless we agree in a separate writing. If an appeal becomes necessary, appellate representation will require a separate engagement letter.

2. Who Will Do the Work.

I will be the partner responsible for the Matter. Elena Duarte will serve as the principal associate. We may staff additional lawyers, paralegals, and litigation-support personnel as the Matter requires, and we will use reasonable efforts to staff it efficiently.

3. Fees.

Our fees are based on the time spent by the lawyers and other professionals who work on the Matter, at the hourly rates in effect when the services are performed. Our current rates are $695 per hour for partners, $410 per hour for associates, and $215 per hour for paralegals. We review and adjust our rates annually, generally effective each January 1, and we will notify you in writing at least thirty (30) days before any adjustment takes effect. Time is recorded in increments of one-tenth of an hour.

The Firm has not made, and cannot make, any promise or guarantee about the outcome of the Matter, and nothing in this letter should be understood as such a promise. Any estimate of fees we may give you is an estimate only and is not a cap on fees.

4. Costs and Expenses.

In addition to fees, you will be responsible for costs and expenses we advance or incur on your behalf, including filing fees, deposition transcripts, expert witness fees, electronic-discovery vendor charges, court reporter fees, travel, and delivery charges. We will bill these at our actual cost. Any single expense expected to exceed $10,000 will be submitted to you for approval before it is incurred.

5. Retainer.

You will deposit $75,000 with the Firm as an advance payment retainer. We will hold the retainer in our client trust account (IOLTA) at Buckeye Fifth Bank, and we will apply it against fees and expenses as they are billed. The retainer is not an estimate of total fees. Any unearned portion of the retainer will be refunded to you at the conclusion of the representation. You agree to replenish the retainer to $75,000 upon our written request if the balance falls below $25,000.

6. Billing and Payment.

We will send you a statement each month describing the services performed, the time expended, and the costs incurred. Statements are due and payable within thirty (30) days of the invoice date. Balances not paid within sixty (60) days may bear interest at the rate of one percent (1%) per month. If a statement remains unpaid for more than ninety (90) days, we may, after giving you reasonable notice and to the extent permitted by the Ohio Rules of Professional Conduct and any applicable court rule, withdraw from the representation.

7. Conflicts of Interest.

We have run a conflicts check against our records and have identified no conflict that prevents us from undertaking the Matter. The Firm represents many clients, and it is possible that during the engagement we may be asked to represent another client in a matter adverse to you but unrelated to the Matter. You agree that we may do so, provided that the other matter is not substantially related to the Matter, we have not obtained confidential information from you that is material to that matter, and we implement an ethical screen. You may withhold consent in any specific instance, and this advance consent does not apply to litigation against you in the Matter itself. We encourage you to consult independent counsel about this advance waiver before signing.

8. Your Responsibilities.

You agree to be truthful with us, to cooperate, to keep us informed of developments, to provide the documents and information we request, and to preserve all documents and electronically stored information that may be relevant to the Matter. We have separately provided you with a litigation-hold notice, and your prompt implementation of it is essential.

9. Confidentiality.

Information you give us in connection with the Matter is protected by the attorney-client privilege and by our duty of confidentiality under Rule 1.6 of the Ohio Rules of Professional Conduct. We will not disclose it except as you authorize or as the Rules permit or require.

10. File Retention.

At the conclusion of the Matter we will return your original documents on request. We will retain the balance of the file for seven (7) years after the Matter is closed, after which the Firm may destroy it without further notice to you.

11. Termination.

You may terminate the representation at any time, with or without cause, by written notice to us. We may withdraw to the extent permitted by the Ohio Rules of Professional Conduct and any applicable court order. If the representation ends before the Matter concludes, you remain responsible for fees and expenses incurred through the date the representation ends.

12. Dispute Resolution.

If a dispute arises between us regarding fees, you may have the right to have the dispute resolved through a fee-arbitration program administered by the local bar association, and we will inform you of that right at the time. Any other dispute arising out of or relating to this engagement will be governed by Ohio law and resolved exclusively in the state or federal courts sitting in Franklin County, Ohio, and each of us consents to the personal jurisdiction of those courts. Nothing in this paragraph waives any right you have to a jury trial, and nothing in it limits the Firm’s obligations under the Ohio Rules of Professional Conduct.

13. No Guarantee; Professional Liability Insurance.

The Firm maintains professional liability insurance in an amount not less than $10,000,000 per claim. Nothing in this letter limits the Firm’s liability to you for malpractice, and we have not asked you to agree to any such limitation.

14. Entire Agreement.

This letter and the attached Standard Terms of Engagement are the entire agreement between us about this engagement and supersede any earlier discussions. Any change must be in a writing signed by both of us.

If the foregoing is acceptable, please sign below and return one copy to me. We are glad to be working with you.

Very truly yours,

HARLOW & VANCE LLP

/s/ Marcus T. Harlow
Marcus T. Harlow
Partner

AGREED AND ACCEPTED:

NORTHGATE INSTRUMENT COMPANY
